solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Handyman sailor left old sea raft in new condition

parts.note: Jack, or Jack Tar, is an old name for a sailor

indicators.note: the letters are put into a fresh state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor abandons an old raft and fixes it up as good as new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' reads as describing the raft but joins the letters 'in new condition' rearranges, along with the L from 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who turns their hand to many small jobs is a general handyman, the stock phrase for one.

clue.text: Chap gets stuck in a state of nervous excitement

parts.note: Jim is a man's name, so any chap
something that jams gets stuck

explanation.surface: A man trapped somewhere works himself into a nervous frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap gets stuck' reads as a sentence: the chap is JIM and 'gets stuck' is JAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: The jitters, a fit of nerves, is the colloquial meaning of this informal word.

clue.text: Preserve shell of one boat

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in a tin

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word one, its shell

explanation.surface: Keep the hull of a single vessel intact.
explanation.definitionFit: A light paddled craft is a kind of small boat.

clue.text: Official flag is blue

parts.note: Off. is a standard abbreviation for official
a regiment's colour is its flag

explanation.surface: The authorised banner is coloured blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' here means risqué or smutty, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean slightly indecent or improper, as with a smutty joke.

clue.text: Refers to an obscene broadcast on Sunday

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the words are sounded

parts.note: obscene means lewd, so 'a lewd'

explanation.surface: Someone mentions an indecent programme aired on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals that 'a lewd' is said out loud, giving the sound of ALLUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention indirectly or hint at something is to refer to it.

clue.text: Support friend in accordance with rules

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Backing a friend while staying within the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting lawfully means acting in line with the rules.

clue.text: Bounder has empty squat as sleeping place

parts.note: a kangaroo, roo for short, bounds along

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its inside, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cad moves into an empty squat for somewhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like a cad, but it is a kangaroo, something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch to sleep, so it is a sleeping place.

clue.text: Pleased to land in river delta

indicators.note: the landing word is placed inside the river and delta letters

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to light on something is to land on it
delta is D in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Happy to come ashore in a river delta.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very pleased or thrilled is a close synonym.

clue.text: Odd gangster, robbed of a grand, goes berserk

indicators.note: going wild signals the remaining letters are scrambled
the word gangster loses a letter, robbed of it

parts.note: G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A peculiar mobster, relieved of a thousand, flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'robbed of' removes G from GANGSTER, leaving ANGSTER, which 'goes berserk' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and peculiar are straight synonyms.

clue.text: Attentive minister's department's nearly perfect

parts.note: Min. is an abbreviation for minister or ministry
D stands for department

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: full can mean complete, perfect

explanation.surface: A minister's office is almost flawless in its attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heedful and aware of something is to be attentive to it.

clue.text: Good oarsman skirts tip of loose iceberg

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round it, so the rower word surrounds the tip

parts.note: an oarsman is a rower

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A capable rower steers round the edge of a drifting iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: A small iceberg barely showing above water is called this by sailors, from its growling sound.

clue.text: Glandular trouble almost laid one out

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A gland problem nearly knocked someone out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glandular trouble' looks like the definition, but 'trouble' starts the wordplay; 'out' rearranges LAID ONE into ENOIDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adenoids are glands at the back of the nose, so the adjective relates to glandular tissue.

clue.text: Inwardly Antigone is cross

indicators.note: inwardly points to letters inside the name Antigone

explanation.surface: The heroine of Sophocles' tragedy is secretly angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry; it is a noun, a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is a hybrid of a male tiger and a lioness, a cross between species.

clue.text: In shops criminal diverts funds

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A crooked shopkeeper skims money off the takings.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain money off dishonestly is to divert it, a figurative use of drawing liquid through a tube.

clue.text: Cable supplier's centre provides this in abbreviated form

definitions.text: Cable supplier's centre provides this in abbreviated form

parts.words: Cable supplier's centre provides this in abbreviated form
parts.note: the middle letters of supplier are P and L, the abbreviation for this kind of electricity cable

explanation.surface: A cable company's headquarters issues something in shortened form.
explanation.walkthrough: The central letters of 'supplier' are PL, which is the short form of the answer, a cable carrying electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhead or buried cable that carries electricity from the supplier is this, abbreviated PL.

clue.text: In confusion, Chay has obligation — to be such a one?

definitions.text: In confusion, Chay has obligation — to be such a one?

indicators.note: confusion means the letters of the name Chay are jumbled

parts.note: a tie is a binding obligation

explanation.surface: Chay Blyth, the British round-the-world sailor, is bound to be a keen sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Chay Blyth is a famous British yachtsman, so the whole clue describes him as well as building the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal Australian and New Zealand word for a yachtsman, which Chay Blyth certainly is.

clue.text: Agreement reached when official count includes ONS

indicators.note: includes means the census word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a census is an official count of the population

explanation.surface: The Office for National Statistics (ONS), Britain's statistics body, joins the census and everyone agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: General agreement among a group is a shared view.

clue.text: Gains from conflict among communists

indicators.note: among puts the conflict word inside the communists word

parts.note: Reds is a common name for communists
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Profits from fighting among left-wing revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Things earned or received as returns are gains.

clue.text: Foundation incorporated British in charge of computerised machine

indicators.note: incorporated means taken in, so the British letter goes inside

parts.note: a root is the foundation of something

explanation.surface: A company founded with British backing runs an automated machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to an automated, computer-controlled machine.

clue.text: Training run plus PE makes one more lithe

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: physical education, as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Exercise, a jog and gym classes leave someone more flexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' looks like part of the fitness picture but rearranges R, PLUS and PE.
explanation.definitionFit: More flexible or lithe is the comparative of an adjective meaning bendy.

clue.text: With a guilty look witch swallows head of newt — and tail

indicators.note: swallows means the witch word takes in another letter

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: A sheepish witch gulps down a newt's head and its tail too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' looks like the newt's tail, but it is a verb meaning follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamefaced, guilty expression is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Hot water starts to run through heating system in homes

parts.note: H is an abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ea is an old word for a river or stream

indicators.note: starts takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Hot water runs round the central heating in houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for the home itself, as in hearth and home.

clue.text: Flying gnats surround head of young male athlete

indicators.note: surround means the scrambled letters go round the others
flying insects whirl about, so the letters are scrambled
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cloud of gnats buzzes round a young man's head while he trains.
explanation.definitionFit: One who performs on bars and floor is a type of athlete.

clue.text: Moor's origin discussed

indicators.note: discussed means spoken out, so the word is heard

parts.note: birth is a beginning or origin

explanation.surface: The background of Othello, the Moor, is being debated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like a noun for a North African, but it is the verb to tie up a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a ship is to bring it into its mooring place at a dock.

clue.text: He is about right: they do succeed

indicators.note: about means the words go round the other letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is roughly correct about those who achieve success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means to follow on, inherit, not to achieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who inherit a title follow, or succeed, the holder.

clue.text: Place to store silverware or most of pot metal maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests another arrangement of the letters
most of means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Somewhere to keep the family silver, or perhaps a heap of pewter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims POT to PO; 'maybe' then rearranges OR, PO and METAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand house keeps its silver plate and cutlery in a dedicated room.

clue.text: Sacred syllable for example has a conclusion

parts.note: om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hinduism and Buddhism

explanation.surface: A holy chant, for instance, comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Frivolous jaunt cut through centre of Milan

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a short jaunt
via means by way of, through

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A light-hearted outing is cut short passing through central Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Of little importance or silly, frivolous and trifling are synonyms.

clue.text: Are conservationists finally determined to give back piece in mosaic

indicators.note: giving back sends the letters back, reading them from the end
finally takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: set means determined or resolved

explanation.surface: Eco-campaigners finally resolve to return a fragment of an old mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give back' reverses ARE, S and SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Each small square tile set into a mosaic is called by this Latin-derived name.

clue.text: Artfully sister creates a new fabric that is wrinkle-free

indicators.note: artfully means arranged with craft, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A sister cleverly designs a novel cloth that never crumples.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric treated so it does not crease or wrinkle is described this way.
